definitions.explanation: An ancient pole weapon with a blade or pointed head, used in Japan and elsewhere before firearms. Largely a historical or literary term in modern Japanese.

examples.japanese: ⟦{古代|こだい}→古代：05324_kodai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{武器|ぶき}→武器：03605_buki⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧{矛|ほこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われた→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Spears were used as ancient weapons.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{山車|だし}→山車：12405_dashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧{矛|ほこ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飾|かざ}られている→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: A large halberd is displayed on the festival float.

examples.japanese: ⟦{議論|ぎろん}→議論：02650_giron⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{矛|ほこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{失言|しつげん}→失言：12189_shitsugen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{向|む}けた→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧。
examples.english: He turned the spear of his argument toward his opponent's slip of the tongue.

notes:
In modern Japanese, {矛|ほこ} is rarely used as a physical noun outside historical or festival contexts. It appears most often in set phrases and idioms.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {矛|ほこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{収|おさ}める→収める：02022_osameru⟧: to end a fight; to lay down arms (literally, to sheathe the spear)
- {矛|ほこ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{向|む}ける→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧: to turn one's attack toward; to target with criticism
- {矛|ほこ}{先|さき}: the point of attack; the brunt of an argument or criticism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {槍|やり}: spear — the everyday word for a spear; more concrete and still occasionally used
- ⟦{刀|かたな}→刀：02194_katana⟧: sword — different category of weapon, with a long curved blade
